newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET - SRI LANKA HAVE BEST CREDENTIALS IN INDEPENDENCE CUP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - SRI LANKA HAVE BEST CREDENTIALS IN INDEPENDENCE CUP.

text.p: World champions Sri Lanka, who defeated a full-strength Pakistan side to win the Sharjah Cup, appear the team with the best credentials in the four-nation Independence Cup starting on Friday.

India are in transition, Pakistan's three leading strike bowlers -- Wasim Akram, Waqar Younis and Mushtaq Ahmed -- are contracted to county cricket while New Zealand will be playing out of season in tropical weather.

Sri Lanka have dropped newscomers Russell Arnold, Nuwan Zoysa and Jayantha Silva from the team who defeated Pakistan. Fast-medium bowler Dulip Liyange plus all-rounders Ruwan Kalpage and Upul Chandana have been named in a squad of 14.

The tournament commemorating 50 years of Indian independence will mark the extension of the subcontinent's cricket season into summer, besides reviving an exchange of tours between India and Pakistan, suspended for political reasons since 1989.

India last toured Pakistan under Krishnamachari Srikkanth in 1989 but a return visit has been cancelled three times since, except for a one-off quarter-final that Pakistan lost at Bangalore during the World Cup last year.
The Independence Cup, which runs from May 9 to 28, will have a round-robin league with the top two teams qualifying for a best-of-three finals. All matches will be day-night ties.
The home side, responding to dismal performances on tours to South Africa and the West Indies, have dropped former captain Mohammed Azharuddin.

Left-hander Vinod Kambli, left out of last year's English tour on disciplinary grounds, has been recalled but paceman Javagal Srinath is unfit while opener Navjot Singh Sidhu has pulled out with a hamstring injury.
